post.title: In 2018, vanilla cost more per kilo than silver. Why?
post.ig:
In 2018, vanilla hit about $600 a kilo, more than silver (about $505 a kilo that year).

Every vanilla flower is pollinated by hand on the one day it opens; pods ripen about 9 months, then cure for months.
Madagascar grew about 42% of the world's vanilla in 2023, so a 2017 cyclone there sent prices soaring.
After Madagascar dropped its $250/kg export floor in 2023, its exports averaged about $48/kg in 2024.
Example (hypothetical, beans only): a gallon of US-standard extract needs 13.35 oz of beans: $227.08 at $600/kg vs $18.17 at $48/kg.
Less than 1% of vanilla flavor comes from real beans.

Sources: BBC (2018); USGS/Silver Institute (2018 silver avg); FAOSTAT via Choices (AAEA); Mintec (2023); Madagascar export trade data 2018-2024; 21 CFR 169; C&EN (ACS).

Hand pollination, about 9 months on the vine, months of curing, and Madagascar's roughly 42% share of world production (FAOSTAT, 2023) explain the price; after Madagascar dropped its $250/kg export floor in 2023, its exports averaged about $48/kg in 2024. Less than 1% of vanilla flavor comes from real beans (C&EN). News and education, not financial advice.
